creationPrompt:
Create a messaging guide for me as a Claw Me Page. Include lead with the task, adapt without drifting, claims to avoid. Replace illustrative data, preserve relevant evidence and uncertainty, and check totals or percentages. Ask only for missing information in one concise batch: brand, audience, actual offer, core message, supporting evidence, tone and prohibited claims.

Use the Claw Me source at https://github.com/clawdotme/plugin in templates/messaging-guide/index.html and templates/_shared/tailwind/README.md. Preserve Archivo, Bitter, the shared theme tokens, and accessible contrast. Author scoped Tailwind 3.4.19 components and compile bundled CSS; do not use a browser CDN. Use semantic responsive HTML, working section links, and useful native details/summary interactions. No scripts, forms, tracking, or embedded frames in the static Page. Deliver matching HTML and PDF from the same content, expand disclosures for print, and inspect page breaks. Use a readable portrait PDF. PDF export is separate from Page publishing unless the current platform explicitly supports it.

exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: A messaging guide with a core promise, supporting points, proof requirements, and examples.
exampleAnswers.Working context: This fictional studio’s message is about clear scope and useful handover. The guide helps collaborators describe the service consistently without claiming outcomes that have not been measured.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Message layer: Core promise · Working wording: A website your next owner can maintain · Support needed: Handover example
Message layer: Scope · Working wording: Five agreed pages, clearly reviewed · Support needed: Defined deliverables
Message layer: Process · Working wording: One feedback owner and two review rounds · Support needed: Working agreement
Message layer: Proof · Working wording: See the café handover sample · Support needed: Approved example
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Lead with the task: For an owner preparing a first website, explain what they receive and how the project proceeds. “A five-page website with an update guide” says more than “a transformative digital experience.”
Adapt without drifting: A short headline can emphasize the handover; a proposal can explain responsibilities and acceptance. Both should describe the same actual service.
Claims to avoid: Do not invent customer counts, awards, conversion improvements, or guaranteed results. When real evidence becomes available, attach its source and the conditions under which it was observed.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: campaign layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
